cd canopy && ws=""; for f in $(git diff --relative --name-only HEAD~1 HEAD -- .); do case "$f" in web/*) ws="$ws web";; server/*) ws="$ws server";; shared/*|package.json|package-lock.json|tsconfig*.json) ws="$ws web server";; esac; done; [ -n "$ws" ] || { echo "the change touches no canopy workspace (web, server or shared)" >&2; exit 1; }; for w in $(printf "%s\n" $ws | sort -u); do NODE_ENV=test npm run -w "$w" test || exit 1; done

planning.reach: Reach: for every behaviour the fix changes, the basis of that decision names each caller and lifecycle path that depends on the old behaviour (server request handlers, session and auth hooks, the BFF proxy to BanyanDB, startup and graceful shutdown, React effects and their cleanup on unmount, query-cache invalidation, thrown errors and rejected promises, timers and retries), starting with the changed module's own startup, shutdown and cleanup paths, and the test that covers it; a path no test covers is stated there as a risk. For a wait the fix makes longer or unbounded, say what happens when the awaited promise never settles or the request is aborted.
planning.e2e: the Playwright end-to-end tests (canopy/e2e, `npm run e2e`)
notes: Canopy is an npm workspace under canopy/ (web, server, shared); every command runs from canopy/. The regression test is a Vitest test in canopy/server/test/ or beside the code in canopy/web/src/ (`*.test.tsx`); give its path from the repository root, as in canopy/server/test/config.test.ts, and its full name (its describe titles and its own title, joined by single spaces). Playwright specs under canopy/e2e are not run as the regression test.
Tests run with NODE_ENV=test; React's test utilities fail under NODE_ENV=production, so do not run a test with the environment's own NODE_ENV.
A change to canopy/shared affects both web and server: the checks run both workspaces' tests.

implementation.conventions: Follow canopy's conventions: strict TypeScript, ESLint as configured per workspace, React function components with hooks, Fastify plugins in the server, and the Apache license header on every new source file. Keep changes under canopy/.
implementation.checks: The controller checks your change in clean checkouts: the base commit with only your test files must fail the test by assertion; the full change must pass the test, the tests of every changed canopy workspace, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` in canopy/ (the cheap checks, which run first), and only then `npm run build`, `npm test` for all workspaces and `make license-dep` with `make check-license-outputs`. Do not change canopy/package-lock.json unless you add a dependency, and then name it in your record's scope exceptions. canopy/LICENSE and canopy/licenses are generated by `make license-dep`: when you add or change a dependency, run it and commit the result (you may write those paths).
selfCheck: cd canopy && ws=$(git ls-files -m -o --exclude-standard | cut -d/ -f1 | sort -u | tr "\n" " "); case " $ws " in *" shared "*) ws="shared web server";; esac; for w in $ws; do case "$w" in web|server|shared) npm run -w "$w" typecheck || exit 1;; esac; case "$w" in web|server) npm run -w "$w" lint || exit 1;; esac; done
implementation.cleanCheckHint: make license-dep regenerates canopy/licenses; after a dependency change run it and commit the result

review.testFiles: Vitest test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.test.tsx`) and Playwright specs and fixtures under `canopy/e2e`
rules: Beyond the diff's own correctness, review what the change breaks.

For every behaviour the change alters, search for each caller and lifecycle path that depends on the old behaviour: request handlers and hooks, session and authentication, startup and shutdown, React effects and their cleanup, cache invalidation, thrown errors and rejected promises, timers and retries.

Report at high severity: a path whose behaviour changes without a test in this change covering it; a removed guarantee (a bound, a timeout, a cleanup, an authorization check, a cancellation) that other code or comments still rely on; a comment that describes a guarantee the change removed; a test whose expected value is derived from the new code rather than from the issue; a change to a session, cookie or API contract between canopy/web and canopy/server without both sides updated.
Report at medium severity a promise that is neither awaited nor handled, an effect or timer without cleanup, and a dependency added without its license artifacts.
